newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 5.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364.

Indonesia regrets the U.S. attack on Iraq, Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said. Alatas said he hoped that both sides would think carefully before things got worse. He also said that Indonesia respects the national rights of Iraq.

President Suharto's son Hutomo Mandala Putra, better known as Tommy, said that Japan's plans to take the Indonesian government to the World Trade Organisation over the contreversial Timor national car policy was a complete waste of time. He said that Japanese firms should concentrate instead on increasing their use of local components.

Jakarta urged the World Trade Organisation (WTO) yesterday to help poorer countries. Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said that some countries in the Asia-Pacific region are experiencing problems in adjusting their laws to those of the WTO. He was talking at a senior ministers meeting in Jakarta aimed at paving the way for the upcoming WTO meeting in Singapore this December.
The Indonesian capital market supervisory agency (Bapepam) may not approve a proposal by majority shareholders of three firms in the Lippo Group for cross-holding of shares.
